body.heading: Choose a journey
paragraphs: Pick a journey you make all the time — from your bed to the kitchen, or from your door to the gate. Guess how many steps it takes. Write your guess down.
Now walk it slowly and count every step out loud. Heel to toe, steady steps — no giant leaps, unless leaping is the experiment.

body.heading: Compare and wonder
paragraphs: Was the real number bigger or smaller than your guess? Steps are a measuring tool you always carry with you.
Ask your adult to walk the same journey and count their steps. Their number will be smaller, because grown-up legs are longer.

body.heading: Map your world in steps
paragraphs: Count more journeys and write them all down: 24 steps to the bathroom, 61 steps to the letterbox. You are making a map measured in you.
Long ago, people measured land in steps and feet. Your expedition uses the oldest measuring tool in the world.

takeaway: Your steps are a measuring tool you always carry, and counting journeys turns your home into a map.
safetyNotes: Count steps only in safe places with your adult, away from traffic. Look up often so you do not bump into things.
screenFreeExtension: Guess before you count — estimating first makes the real number a surprise.
